symptom: The full Vitest run could not execute the serialized generation-motion probe after token consolidation.
direct_cause: The serialized function referenced a module import in the destination browser realm.
class_root: The single owner of the live media preference must also support execution without module capture.
affected_population: Generation badges and live accessibility preference subscribers
internal_only_reason: Existing Playwright evaluate and the September probe contract define transport semantics. The rendering engine and its APIs are unchanged.
invariants: A standalone browser function reads the actual target-window preference and releases any temporary WebGL context.
Query-only consumers observe a live MediaQueryList without creating a canvas.

door_reduction.why_not: Preference consumers require both reactive and immediate reads; the generation renderer and direct automation additionally need the complete snapshot. They now all use a single query in the same browser primitive.

generality_proof: The complete reader has no external runtime symbol. A query-only request returns before the WebGL path, while existing callers retain the no-argument snapshot.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Resolve browser capabilities in the calling realm and release the temporary GPU context.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Existing serializable entry is an export of the browser primitive.
Returns the media query directly and does not allocate a WebGL context.

recurrence.reason: A future import inside a callback serialized by value will again be unavailable in a separate realm.
same_class_scan: git grep readProcessMotionCapability plus door-map readBrowserMotion reducedMotionQuery; checked generation hook, Agent row and standalone Playwright evaluation.

prevention.invariant: Both supported browser reads originate from a standalone function using the target realm’s own APIs.
prevention.failure_mode: Absent matchMedia yields false; an unavailable renderer remains null and the process policy selects a static surface.
prevention.strategy: Preserve the cross-realm entry as an alias of the single browser reader and exercise it inside a separate Chromium page.

legacy_paths.rationale: Removed the reader that relied on a captured import; its public name still resolves to the standalone primitive.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Application-owned function transport uses the existing standard browser APIs and existing Playwright.

migration: Existing no-argument calls and the returned capability fields are preserved. No persisted schema changes.
residual_risks: Runtime GPU switching inside the same Document still follows the existing document cache.

invariant_owner_layer.why: Full reads and preference-only reads both run at this boundary.
